At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.
goal.verificationContract:

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

(3) checkboxes match code (each task.md flip carries a Verified note with its command output). (6) Reviewer 8.2 compared artifacts to implementation across the complete 17-file diff + 3 new tests: all 6 checklist items PASS, verdict OK with notes; findings MINOR1 + NOTE1 fixed (conjoined static_assert; setMolecule unlocks+deletes abandoned m_qube), NOTE2/NOTE3 recorded report-only. (7) Tree coherent: change committed and pushed (3c17884c0, 73099eb46, f0537fb89); working tree retains only pre-existing build-asan/ deletions and .pi scratch unrelated to the change. findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. (3) checkboxes match code (each task.md flip carries a Verified note with its command output). (4) Builds/tests: local full suite 40/40 under xvfb; Linux CI success on both change commits; Windows Installer CI success (run 41279274144) after fixing the C2487 the first run caught. (6) Reviewer 8.2 compared artifacts to implementation across the complete 17-file diff + 3 new tests: all 6 checklist items PASS, verdict OK with notes; findings MINOR1 + NOTE1 fixed (conjoined static_assert; setMolecule unlocks+deletes abandoned m_qube), NOTE2/NOTE3 recorded report-only. findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

Document switch mid-calculation stays safe — copy/ESP workers quiesced in setMolecule; abandoned write-locked cube now released in the quiesce block instead of deleted while locked (reviewer NOTE 1 fixed)

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed
Lobes generate sequentially; cube data is single-precision; meshes move into Mesh with one write-lock and one revision bump

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

Test-driven fix: the density contraction read stale scratch for screened-out shells; buffer now zeroed per point. Parallel marching cubes is slab-deterministic with K=1↔K=4 output equivalent as vertex multisets — meshgenparallelTest 4/4

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

While the Windows verification ran, it caught a pre-existing MSVC C2487 in ModernRendererBackend (member-level A_EXPORT inside an already-exported class, from the archived parity change) — fixed and both CIs now green on the pushed tree

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The surface/orbital visualization performance change is fully implemented, reviewed, and verified — GUI no longer blocks on grid/vertex-sized work, memory is bounded (334 MB peak for a Very-High orbital surface vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before), marching cubes is parallel+deterministic, evaluation is distance-screened (~2× at 0.15 Å, more on larger systems), and background precalculation is clamped at Medium. Changed: 17 source files across gaussianset, the surface/orbital extensions, cube/mesh/meshgenerator, glwidget, plus three new headless tests (screening, parallel-mesh, precalc-policy); committed as 3c17884c0 + 73099eb46 (MSVC C2487 fix the Windows run caught in pre-existing parity-change code) + f0537fb89 (evidence records). Evidence: OpenSpec reports all_done with 0 remaining tasks; two independent reviewer checkpoints (OK, no blockers) with all findings integrated; Linux Qt6 CI green and Windows Installer CI green on the pushed tree. Tests: full ctest suite under xvfb 40/40 passed; screeningtest 5/5, meshgenparallelTest 4/4, precalcpolicyTest 5/5. Unresolved: the four pointer-driven manual-matrix rows (app feel during load/calc, real drag feel, ≤0.3 s surface return) need a human driving the real app — every headlessly checkable aspect is covered and recorded in tasks.md. Next: human confirmation of the manual-matrix rows during normal app use; OpenSpec archive of the change when satisfied.

findingGroups.title: GUI responsiveness (D1/D3/D4)
findings: GUI never blocks on surface work — cube-calc setup, grid copy, and ESP coloring run on workers with epoch-guarded continuations; reviewer checklist verified lock pairing GUI→GUI and no grid-proportional GUI calls remain

findingGroups.title: Bounded memory (D5/D6)
findings: Very-High orbital surface peaks at 334 MB total (0.05 Å, 7.5M-point grid, 64,928-triangle lobes) vs ~0.5+ GB transient reserve before; measured with a temporary probe on the caffeine fixture, then removed

findingGroups.title: Faster math (D7/D8/D9)
findings: Distance screening cuts the 0.15 Å MO cube from 76 ms to 39 ms (speedup grows with system size); screened vs unscreened agree within 1e-9 on both MO and density paths — screeningtest 5/5

findingGroups.title: Render path (D10)
findings: Surfaces hide during drags and return ~250 ms after release; backface culling halves fill cost for closed lobes; single VBO upload per assembled mesh; resolved GL profile logged at startup

findingGroups.title: Precalculation policy (D11)
findings: Background precalculation is clamped at Medium via OrbitalWidget::clampPrecalcQuality with a real conjoined enum-order static_assert (reviewer caught the chained-< pin as vacuous) — precalcpolicyTest 5/5; explicit per-orbital quality path untouched

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1.1 setDefaultFormat before QApplication (main.cpp:219 before :221); testContext grep empty; warning count 0 on 10.66.0.12 fixed run (present in baseline). 1.2 baseline on 10.66.0.12 reproduced profile Core + giant methane; fixed build: warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, root-display screenshot captured; compat resolution demonstrated on local llvmpipe (4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). 2.1 tierSupportedAt profile gating; forced-path stale-copy fix. 2.2 renderertiertest 11/11. 2.3 forced-tier diagnostics unit-tested + live-observed. 3.1 initializeGL Core skip + one-time diagnostic observed once per run. 3.2 glpainter coreFixedFunctionAvailable guards every fixed-function entry; 0 GL error spam. 4.1 ctest 40/40 xvfb + offscreen + asan. 4.2 matrix per owner scope (10.66.0.12 Core case + local compat case). 4.3 Windows Installer run 41346998329 success 57m58s on final commit; Linux CI 41346990696 success 40m25s. 4.4 reviewer round 2 verdict OK, all findings applied in b70e3a619, suite re-verified. openspec instructions apply: 11/11 complete, 0 remaining; working tree clean at b61513a53.
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. The Camera-matrix decoupling that would make the modern tier render correctly on core-only drivers (like 10.66.0.12's nouveau) is design.md's documented follow-up non-goal.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.
